crash.analysis.driver.steps:
Install the newest driver from the website of your graphics card maker (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel), not through Windows Update.
Restart the computer after installing.
On laptops: let Minecraft use the dedicated graphics card (Windows Settings › System › Display › Graphics).
Start again.
crash.analysis.driver.what: The graphics driver crashed while Minecraft was drawing.
crash.analysis.driver.why: The crash happened inside the graphics driver, not in Minecraft or Lumora. Old or broken drivers are the most common reason.
crash.analysis.driver_switch.steps:
Let Lumora switch the render backend to Vulkan (button below).
If it keeps crashing: install the newest graphics driver from the website of your graphics card maker and restart the computer.
You can switch back under Settings › Game › Graphics backend.
crash.analysis.driver_switch.what: The graphics driver crashed while Minecraft was drawing with OpenGL.
crash.analysis.driver_switch.why: The crash happened inside the graphics driver. This Minecraft version can also draw with Vulkan, which uses a different part of the driver.
crash.analysis.exit.steps:
Use "Repair & play": Lumora checks all files, Java and itself and starts again.
Close other programs that use a lot of memory or the graphics card.
If it happens again, copy the report for support ("Copy for support").
crash.analysis.exit.what: Minecraft ended suddenly without writing a crash report.
crash.analysis.exit.why: This usually means the Java process was ended from outside or crashed natively: a driver problem, too little memory or damaged files.
crash.analysis.files.steps:
Use "Repair & play": Lumora downloads the damaged files again and checks them.
If it happens again: check the free disk space under Settings › Storage.
crash.analysis.files.what: A file of the game could not be read.
crash.analysis.files.why: A downloaded file is damaged or incomplete, for example after an interrupted download or a full disk.
crash.analysis.java.steps:
Use "Repair & play": Lumora installs the Java version this Minecraft version needs.
If you set your own Java under Settings, remove it there.
crash.analysis.java.what: Minecraft was started with a Java version that is too old.
crash.analysis.java.why: Part of the game needs a newer Java than the one used for this start.
crash.analysis.lumora_mixin.steps:
Use "Repair & play": Lumora installs its client for this version again.
If it crashes again in the same place, it is most likely a Lumora bug: copy the report ("Copy for support") and send it to the Lumora team.
crash.analysis.lumora_mixin.what: Lumora could not hook into Minecraft at one place.
crash.analysis.lumora_mixin.why: Lumora's own code is named in the report. Either its files do not match this Minecraft version (fixed by a repair) or it is a bug in Lumora.
crash.analysis.memory.steps:
Let Lumora raise the maximum memory to {0} (button below).
Close other programs while playing.
Use fewer or smaller resource packs and a lower render distance.
crash.analysis.memory.why: The game needed more memory than it was allowed to use ("OutOfMemoryError"), for example because of a high render distance, big resource packs or many mods.
crash.analysis.memory_full.steps:
Close other programs while playing.
Lower the render distance and use fewer or smaller resource packs.
More memory for Minecraft does not help any more: your computer does not have more to spare.
crash.analysis.memory_full.why: The game needed more memory than it was allowed to use, and it already gets as much as makes sense on this computer.
crash.analysis.mismatch.steps:
Use "Repair & play": Lumora checks all files and replaces the ones that do not belong to this version.
If you added mods yourself, remove them and try again.
crash.analysis.mismatch.what: Parts of the game do not fit together.
crash.analysis.mismatch.why: The game looked for code that is missing or different, usually a file from another version.
crash.analysis.mod.steps:
Disable {0} (button below) and start again.
If the game then runs, look for a newer version of {0} that fits this Minecraft version.
crash.analysis.mod.why: {0} is named most often in the error, so it is the most likely cause.
crash.analysis.mod_mismatch.steps:
Disable {0} (button below) and start again.
Then look for the version of {0} that is made for this Minecraft version.
crash.analysis.mod_mismatch.what: {0} does not fit this Minecraft version.
crash.analysis.mod_mismatch.why: {0} uses code that does not exist in this version of the game.
crash.analysis.mod_mixin.steps:
Disable {0} (button below) and start again.
If you need {0}, look for a version for this Minecraft version.
crash.analysis.mod_mixin.what: {0} could not hook into the game.
crash.analysis.mod_mixin.why: {0} tried to change a part of Minecraft that is different in this version.
crash.analysis.none: There is no crash to analyze.
crash.analysis.resources.steps:
Turn off resource packs and shaders one by one in the game and start again.
Use "Repair & play" if it also crashes without them.
crash.analysis.resources.what: Loading resources (textures, sounds or shaders) failed.
crash.analysis.resources.why: Usually a resource pack or shader that does not fit this version, sometimes a damaged file.
crash.analysis.session.steps:
Sign in again (button below).
Then start again.
crash.analysis.session.why: The stored Microsoft session has expired or was rejected by the server.
crash.analysis.system_memory.steps:
Close other programs (browser, Discord, games) while playing.
Let Lumora lower the maximum memory for Minecraft to {0} (button below), so more stays free for Windows.
If your computer has 8 GB or less, also lower the render distance.
crash.analysis.system_memory.what: Your computer ran out of memory.
crash.analysis.system_memory.why: Java could not get memory from Windows: Minecraft and the other open programs together need more than the computer has.
crash.analysis.title: Crash analysis
crash.analysis.unknown.steps:
Use "Repair & play": Lumora checks all files and starts again.
If you added mods yourself, remove them and try again.
If it happens again, copy the report ("Copy for support") and ask for help.
crash.analysis.unknown.what: Minecraft crashed with an error that has no known cause.
crash.analysis.unknown.why: Nothing in the report points clearly to a mod, a driver or the settings.
crash.analysis.vulkan.steps:
Let Lumora switch the render backend to OpenGL (button below).
Install the newest graphics driver; Vulkan needs a current driver.
You can switch back under Settings › Game › Graphics backend.
crash.analysis.vulkan.why: Minecraft could not use Vulkan with this graphics card or driver.
crash.analysis.world.steps:
Do not open the world again until you have a backup.
Open the library: there you can make a backup of the world or restore an older one.
If only one world crashes, the problem is in that world, not in the game.
crash.analysis.world.what: The crash happened while the world was running or loading.
crash.analysis.world.why: Something in the world (a block, an entity or a damaged chunk) caused the error.

perf.preset.balanced.desc: Medium view distance, nice graphics, fewer particles – good visuals at smooth FPS.
perf.preset.max_fps.desc: Short view distance, fast graphics, few particles, no clouds and shadows – for weak PCs and PvP.
perf.preset.quality.desc: Long view distance, all particles, clouds, shadows and V-Sync – for strong PCs.
perf.profile.hint: Changes the video settings in options.txt of this version. The original is backed up first.
perf.profile.quit_game: Please quit Minecraft first – the game overwrites options.txt when it closes.
perf.profile.start_once: Start Minecraft {0} ({1}) once, then the profiles can be applied.
perf.subtitle: More FPS for Minecraft {0} ({1}): graphics profiles, performance mods and Java settings.
play.already_running: Minecraft is already running. Multiple instances can be allowed under Settings → Game.
play.already_running.title: Minecraft is already running
play.error.java_start: The Java process could not be started: {0}
project.deps.hint: Required dependencies are installed with it after you confirm; optional ones only if you tick them.
project.error: The project could not be loaded: {0}
quit.game_running: Minecraft is still running. Close the launcher? The game keeps running.
security.2fa.text: Lumora only signs in through your Microsoft account. So you set up the second step directly at Microsoft, then it protects Minecraft too.
security.authenticator.desc: Microsoft Authenticator or another app with one-time codes
security.sessions.desc: Everything on this PC that has access to your accounts.
security.sessions.empty: No account is signed in on this PC.
security.storage: Each account's sign-in is stored separately encrypted (Windows DPAPI) on this PC. The launcher never stores passwords. You can see devices outside this PC under "Activity at Microsoft".
servers.add.invalid_text: "{0}" is not a valid server address.
servers.add.title: Own server
servers.join.game_running: Quit the running game to join another server.
servers.subtitle: Popular servers and your own, sorted by players online. Numbers come live from each server.
settings.appearance.accent.desc: Color for buttons, selection and highlights throughout the launcher. Takes effect after a restart.
settings.appearance.accent.title: Accent color
settings.appearance.hw.desc: Draws the launcher with the graphics card (Direct3D). Turning it off helps with graphics glitches caused by drivers. Takes effect after a restart.
settings.appearance.hw.title: Hardware acceleration
settings.appearance.motion.desc: No automatic animations (rotating skin preview, loading spinners). Switching pages stays instant.
settings.appearance.motion.title: Reduce motion
settings.appearance.pixel.desc: Like the Lumora menus in the game: pixel font for titles, navigation and buttons, cards and buttons with pixel edges. Off: modern design with round corners. Takes effect after a restart.
settings.appearance.pixel.title: Lumora pixel design
settings.appearance.quick_play.desc: Shows the first five servers from the server list of the selected version under "Play". One click starts the game directly on the server.
settings.appearance.quick_play.title: Quick Play
settings.appearance.snapshots.desc: Also shows the weekly snapshots under "News → Changelog", not only releases.
settings.appearance.snapshots.title: Minecraft snapshots in the changelog
settings.appearance.start_page.desc: The page the launcher shows after opening.
settings.appearance.start_page.title: Start page
settings.chat.badge.desc: Shows the number of unread chats and requests in the sidebar and on the tray icon.
settings.chat.badge.title: Unread counter
settings.chat.notify.desc: What the launcher notifies you about while its window is in the background: messages, requests and hints, or messages only.
settings.chat.notify.title: Notifications
settings.chat.server.desc: Server for friends, groups and chat. Empty = off. On the internet only with wss:// (TLS).
settings.chat.server.title: Lumora social server
settings.chat.share_server.desc: Friends see which server you play on. When off, they only see "Multiplayer". Takes effect the next time you start the game.
settings.chat.share_server.title: Show server address to friends
settings.debug.address.desc: Host and port for JVM debugging, only on this PC (e.g. localhost:5005).
settings.debug.address.invalid: Only this PC is allowed: localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] with a port, e.g. localhost:5005.
settings.debug.address.title: Debug address
settings.debug.client_reset.confirm:
Reset all settings of the Lumora client in the game (modules, HUD, addons, design) to default?

The previous ones stay as a backup "config.backup-…" in the instance folders.
Worlds, options and addon files stay unchanged.
settings.debug.client_reset.desc: Resets all settings of the Lumora client in the game (modules, HUD, addons, design) to default. The previous ones stay as a backup (config.backup-…).
settings.debug.client_reset.done.one: Reset ({0} folder backed up). The defaults apply the next time you start the game.
settings.debug.client_reset.done.other: Reset ({0} folders backed up). The defaults apply the next time you start the game.
settings.debug.client_reset.none: There were no Lumora settings yet.
settings.debug.client_reset.running: Minecraft is running. Quit the game, then reset the settings.
settings.debug.client_reset.title: Reset Lumora client settings
settings.debug.crashes.desc: Crash reports of all versions with likely cause and solutions.
settings.debug.crashes.title: Crashes
settings.debug.diag.desc: System check: Java, graphics, memory, network and game files.
settings.debug.diag.title: Diagnostics
settings.debug.heap.desc: Writes a dump of the game memory to the diagnostics folder when memory runs out. Useful for memory leaks, but the files can be several gigabytes large.
settings.debug.heap.title: Heap dump on out of memory
settings.debug.logs.desc: Launcher and game logs. Credentials are never written.
settings.debug.logs.title: Logs
settings.debug.mode.desc: JVM debugging for the Minecraft process. "Listen" waits for a debugger at startup, "Attach" connects to a debugger that is already running.
settings.debug.mode.title: Debug mode
settings.debug.reset.confirm:
Reset all launcher settings to default?
Accounts, game folders, worlds and the Lumora social server are kept.
settings.debug.reset.desc: Resets memory, Java, window, downloads and display to default.
settings.debug.reset.done: Reset. The display updates after restarting the launcher.
settings.debug.reset.title: Reset settings
settings.debug.restore.desc: Adds instance folders under instances that the launcher no longer knows back as own instances. Existing ones stay, nothing is deleted.
settings.debug.restore.none: All instance folders are already known.
settings.debug.restore.title: Restore instances from disk
settings.debug.threads.desc: If the game does not respond for 30 seconds, Lumora writes the stack traces of all game threads as a report (Crashes). Costs only a few kilobytes of text. Applies from the next start.
settings.debug.threads.title: Thread dump on freeze
settings.game.after_launch.desc: What the launcher does as soon as Minecraft is running.
settings.game.after_launch.title: After launch
settings.game.backend.desc: What Minecraft 26.2 and newer draws with. "Default" lets Minecraft decide (and leaves your in-game choice alone), Vulkan or OpenGL is set on every start. Older versions always use their default.
settings.game.backend.title: Graphics backend
settings.game.env.desc: Variables for the game process, one KEY=VALUE per line or separated by commas.
settings.game.env.invalid: Invalid (format KEY=VALUE, name made of letters, digits and _):
settings.game.env.title: Environment variables
settings.game.fullscreen.desc: Always start Minecraft in fullscreen. When off, your in-game choice is kept.
settings.game.fullscreen.title: Force fullscreen
settings.game.instances.desc: Start Minecraft several times at the same time, also the same version (up to 8 runs per version, e.g. with two accounts). The runs share the version's settings and worlds.
settings.game.instances.title: Multiple instances
settings.game.java.desc: Path to your own Java installation instead of Mojang's official runtime. Only change this if you know what you are doing.
settings.game.java.title: Custom JRE
settings.game.jvm.desc: Default arguments passed to Java at startup.
settings.game.jvm.title: Custom JVM arguments
settings.game.memory.desc: Change with care: less is often more, too little is bad. More than 6 GB rarely helps. Your system has {0} GB.
settings.game.memory.title: Allocated memory
settings.game.patch.desc: Remembers the last chosen sub-version per main version (e.g. 1.21.8 for 1.21), also after a restart. A click on the card selects it again.
settings.game.patch.title: Remember selected patch
settings.game.perf.desc: Optimized garbage collector (G1 with short pauses) against stutters. Skipped if your own JVM arguments choose a different collector.
settings.game.perf.title: Performance improvements
settings.game.resolution.desc: Initial Minecraft window size in pixels. Empty = Minecraft default.
settings.game.resolution.title: Window resolution
settings.game.versions.desc: Which Minecraft versions the version menu shows (as in the installer). Hidden versions keep their worlds and settings.
settings.game.versions.title: Versions in the launcher
settings.general.autostart.desc: Starts the launcher in the tray when you sign in, so friends can reach you in chat while you are at your PC.
settings.general.autostart.failed_on: Autostart could not be set up.
settings.general.autostart.installed_onl: Only available with the installed LumoraLauncher.exe.
settings.general.autostart.title: Start with Windows
settings.general.channel.desc: "Stable" is the right choice for almost everyone. "Pre-release" also offers pre-release versions of the launcher as soon as there are any (also only with a valid signature).
settings.general.channel.title: Update channel
settings.general.data_dir.desc: Lumora data: libraries, Java, Lumora settings, own instances and logs. A change takes effect after a restart.
settings.general.data_dir.moved:
The new data folder will be used after restarting the launcher.
Existing data is not moved.
settings.general.data_dir.title: Data folder
settings.general.downloads.desc: Maximum number of files downloaded at the same time. Higher values can speed up downloads but need more bandwidth. Takes effect after a restart.
settings.general.downloads.title: Simultaneous downloads limit
settings.general.game_dir.desc: All versions without their own instance play here, like Minecraft itself (.minecraft): they share worlds, resource packs, screenshots and options with vanilla. You choose an own instance in the version menu next to "Play".
settings.general.game_dir.title: Default game folder
settings.general.ingame.desc: Chooses the design of the in-game menus: Lumora or classic Minecraft style (as in the installer). Applies the next time any version starts.
settings.general.ingame.title: Customize in-game experience
settings.general.language.desc: Language of the launcher. German and English are complete; mod descriptions stay in their original language. Takes effect after a restart.
settings.general.language.title: Language
settings.general.tray.desc: Closing the window keeps the launcher running in the notification area. You can quit it from the tray icon.
settings.general.tray.title: Stay in the tray when closed
settings.general.update_auto.desc: Looks for new versions of the launcher and the resource packs at startup and asks before every change.
settings.general.update_auto.title: Automatic update check
settings.general.update_direct.desc: If you start the launcher from a pinned taskbar icon or your own shortcut, it still updates itself. Newly pinned icons start LumoraClient.exe. Off: only a start via LumoraClient.exe updates, otherwise you only get a pointer to the release page. Takes effect after a restart.
settings.general.update_direct.title: Update on direct start too
settings.general.version.desc: New versions come from {0} and are only installed with a valid signature.
settings.general.version.title: Launcher version {0}
settings.ingame.question:
What should the in-game menus look like?

Lumora design: Lumora's own menus, buttons and colors.
Minecraft style: Minecraft's own menus and buttons, the Lumora hub stays.

Applies the next time any version starts; can be changed any time in the game under Hub › Themes.
settings.integrations.curseforge.desc: CurseForge only answers with an API key. Lumora has none built in: create your own in the CurseForge for Studios console and enter it here. It is stored encrypted for your Windows user (DPAPI) and never written to a log.
settings.integrations.curseforge.title: CurseForge API key
settings.integrations.discord.desc: Through the Discord app on this PC, Discord shows whether you are in the launcher or what you are playing, e.g. "Lumora 26.3 on someip.net". When off, it only shows "Multiplayer" instead of the server address and its icon.
settings.integrations.discord.title: Show server in Discord
settings.integrations.news.desc: News and patch notes come from Mojang's launcher content (launchercontent.mojang.com), player counts in the server list directly from the servers. No data about you is sent.
settings.integrations.news.title: Minecraft news
settings.integrations.stats.desc: Would share anonymous details such as operating system and version. There is no Lumora statistics server yet: nothing is sent even when it is on.
settings.integrations.stats.title: Anonymous launcher statistics
settings.storage.cache.desc: Downloaded Lumora files are cached once. If the limit is exceeded, the launcher deletes the oldest at startup (they are downloaded again when needed). 0 = no limit.
settings.storage.cache.title: Download cache limit (GB)
settings.storage.logs.desc: The launcher deletes older game logs of own instances at startup by itself (latest.log stays). It leaves the default .minecraft folder untouched.
settings.storage.logs.title: Keep game logs for
settings.storage.usage.desc: Java, download cache, libraries, worlds, mods, logs
settings.storage.usage.title: Storage usage
settings.title: Settings

social.group.leave.owner: The group goes to the longest-serving managing member.
social.group.no_description_manage: No description yet. Add one under Settings.

social.not_friends: You are no longer friends. The history stays readable, new messages cannot be sent.
social.off.confirm: The launcher and the game no longer connect to {0}. Friends and groups stay on the server.
social.off.title: Turn off Lumora Social
social.pick.none: All your friends are already in the group – or you have none yet. Add friends first.
social.pick_chat: Choose a friend or a group on the left.
social.remove_friend.confirm: {0} will be removed from your friends list.

social.role.hint: Edit roles: click a role in the overview. Owner and member are fixed.
social.role.manage: May manage the group: add and remove members, change name and description.
social.server.hint: Lumora Social needs its own server, run by you or a friend (lumora-social-server.jar, see SOCIAL.md). On a local network an IP address is enough, on the internet wss:// (TLS) is required. Messages are stored on this server – whoever runs it can read them.
social.session_expired: Sign-in expired. Please sign in again in the launcher.
social.setup.text: Friends and chats run over your own Lumora social server, run by you or someone in your group (lumora-social-server.jar, guide in SOCIAL.md). There is no preset server. You sign in with your Minecraft account (official Mojang session service); the server sees neither password nor token. Messages are stored on the server.
social.setup.title: Connect to a Lumora social server
social.share_server.tip: Takes effect the next time you start the game: friends see which server you play on.
social.signin.subtitle: Sign in with your Microsoft account to use friends and chats.
social.signin.text: Lumora Social recognizes you by your Minecraft account. After signing in, the launcher connects to the configured server automatically.
social.subtitle: Chat with friends, create groups with roles and see who is playing – in the launcher and in the game.
social.title: Friends & Groups
storage.bar_hint: Hover over the bar to see what each color stands for
storage.clear.confirm:

storage.game_running: Please quit Minecraft first – the game is using these files right now.

storage.kind.libraries.desc: Shared libraries of all versions and loaders

storage.kind.other.desc: Settings, accounts, diagnostics and other game data
storage.kind.runtimes.desc: Downloaded when needed for the versions that need them
storage.kind.versions.desc: Minecraft and loader files of the installed versions
storage.player_data: The launcher does not delete player data
